New independent product-generator DP checked full membership, minimal generators, gap sets, Frobenius, genus and every pseudo-Frobenius gap for all 108 integers 3<=m<=110, always agreeing with the closed formulas. This bounded test corroborates, rather than proves, the unbounded m statement.
correctness.rationale: Ideal multiplication means the additive monoid generated by ordinary products. The positive products of <2,3> and O_m are generated by 2k and 3k (m<=k<2m). Every even integer >=2m lies in the product. Its least odd product is u=3r; an odd sum of at least two nonzero products is >=T=u+2m, and any smaller odd product must have the first odd factor exactly 3 and lies on the finite progression u+6j (0<=j<ceil(m/3)). Every odd integer >=T is u plus a permitted even summand. Hence the claimed complete normal form and unique minimal generators follow. Count parity gaps for F and genus; test adding all minimal generators to each gap to determine the three disjoint pseudo-Frobenius classes, including the m mod 3 exceptional u−2; counting yields type.
risks: Distinguish the additive ideal product from the elementwise product set. The geometric-sequence m=2 boundary is known prior work and not an originality claim.

limitations: The ideal product is additive closure of integer products; only O_2 with O_m (m>=3), not general semiring ideal powers.
